title: Codex runs routine quantum-chip measurements while researchers retain oversight
friendlyTitle: A Codex agent helped run routine tests on a quantum chip
summary: An MIT Engineering Quantum Systems researcher connected GPT-5.6 Sol through Codex to laboratory software for calibrating a six-qubit chip. The agent could choose parameters, run and analyze routine measurements when signals were clear, but weak or noisy results still required experienced guidance.
friendlySummary: The agent operated lab software, measured a chip and adjusted some tests by itself. It worked best with clear signals and still needed an expert when results were noisy or unusual.
whyItMatters: This is a practical pattern for supervised automation: give an agent a defined procedure and tools, let it handle repetitive measurements, and reserve ambiguous evidence and experiment design for specialists. Similar workflows can free time without pretending current agents can replace expert judgment.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI can take over repeated steps while skilled people focus on harder decisions. Keep an expert involved whenever the evidence is unclear.
